en alarmklokke.explanation: "En alarmklokke" means "an alarm bell". It is built from "alarm" (alarm) and "klokke" (bell). The part "klokke" also means "clock" when you ask the time: "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

en albue.explanation: "En albue" means "an elbow". Danish can use "albuen" (the elbow) for your own elbow: "Jeg har slået albuen" (I hit my elbow), literally "I hit the elbow".

en alder.explanation: "En alder" means "an age". To ask how old someone is, Danish does not use "alder". It uses "gammel" (old): "Hvor gammel er du?" (How old are you?) To say "at my age", use "i min alder": "Det er svært i min alder" (It is hard at my age).

en algoritme.explanation: "En algoritme" means "an algorithm". Danish spells it without an "h": "algoritme", not "algorithm".

en alkoholiker.explanation: "En alkoholiker" means "an alcoholic". It is built from "alkohol" (alcohol). Danish spells it with "k", not "c".

en allergi.explanation: "En allergi" means "an allergy". To name what you react to, put its name in front of "allergi" as one word: "en pollenallergi" (a pollen allergy).

en alliance.explanation: "En alliance" means "an alliance". To say who the alliance is with, add "med" (with): "Vi har en alliance med vores naboer" (We have an alliance with our neighbors).

en allieret.explanation: "En allieret" means "an ally". When you talk about history, "de allierede" (the allies) are the countries that fought Germany in World War II: "Danmark blev befriet af de allierede i 1945" (Denmark was freed by the Allies in 1945).

en altan.explanation: "En altan" means "a balcony". The part "altan" is also in "en altankasse" (a balcony planter box): "Jeg har blomster i en altankasse" (I have flowers in a balcony planter box).

en amatør.explanation: "En amatør" means "an amateur". To call a person who does a poor job an amateur, say "Sikke en amatør!" (What an amateur!) This is an insult.

en ambassade.explanation: "En ambassade" means "an embassy". To say you are going to the embassy, use "på" (at): "Vi skal på ambassaden i morgen" (We are going to the embassy tomorrow).

en ambassadør.explanation: "En ambassadør" means "an ambassador". When a well-known person speaks for a cause, the word fits too: "Hun er ambassadør for en velgørenhedsorganisation" (She is an ambassador for a charity).

en ambition.explanation: "En ambition" means "an ambition". To say someone has big goals, use "at have" (to have) and the plural: "De har store ambitioner for firmaet" (They have big ambitions for the firm).

en ambulance.explanation: "En ambulance" means "an ambulance". In Denmark, you call the emergency number 112 to get one: "Ring til 112!" (Call 112!)

en amerikaner.explanation: "En amerikaner" means "an American". It is built from "Amerika" (America). Danish writes it with a small first letter: "amerikaner", not "Amerikaner". In a Danish bakery, "en amerikaner" is also a flat, round cake with icing: "Vi køber to amerikanere hos bageren" (We buy two amerikaner cakes at the baker).

en analyse.explanation: "En analyse" means "an analysis". To say what you analyze, add "af" (of): "Vi laver en analyse af tallene" (We do an analysis of the numbers).

en ananas.explanation: "En ananas" means "a pineapple". Danish doubles the s before an ending, so "the pineapple" is "ananassen" with two s's.

en anbefaling.explanation: "En anbefaling" means "a recommendation". To say who told you about a place, use "på anbefaling af" (on the recommendation of): "Vi kom på anbefaling af en ven" (We came on a friend's recommendation).

en and.explanation: "En and" means "a duck". The form for "the duck" is "anden". The same spelling is also the word for "the other". To talk about the duck, say "Anden svømmer" (The duck swims). To point to the other one of two things, say "Jeg tager den anden" (I take the other one).

en andel.explanation: "En andel" means "a share / portion". To talk about a part of a whole group, use "andelen af" (the share of): "Andelen af ældre vokser" (The share of older people is growing). The word "andel" is also in "en andelsbolig" (a cooperative apartment): "Vi bor i en andelsbolig" (We live in a cooperative apartment).

en andelsbolig.explanation: "En andelsbolig" means "a cooperative apartment". It is built from "andel" (share) and "bolig" (home). In Denmark, the monthly fee you pay for one is called "boligafgift" (housing fee).

en anekdote.explanation: "En anekdote" means "an anecdote". Danish spells it with "k", not "c": "anekdote".

en anelse.explanation: "En anelse" means "a hint / slight idea". To say something is a touch better, put "en anelse" before the describing word: "Det er en anelse bedre" (It is a touch better). To ask whether someone has any idea, say "Har du en anelse om hvorfor?" (Do you have any idea why?)

en anfører.explanation: "En anfører" means "a captain (team)". It comes from the verb "at anføre" (to lead).

en angriber.explanation: "En angriber" means "a forward / attacker". Outside sport, when someone attacks a person, use it for "attacker": "Angriberen løb væk" (The attacker ran away).
